name: Healthcare
blurb: Clinical, administrative, and diagnostic AI, and the rules around it.

points.desc: The WHO guidance on ethics and governance of AI for health is the reference document for member-state health systems.
points.name: WHO set the governance frame

points.desc: NIH's data science and AI programs (including Bridge2AI) fund the datasets and methods clinical AI is built on.
points.name: NIH runs the research infrastructure

points.desc: The Medical Models section tracks clinical and biomedical models by the Hub's own tags.
points.name: Medical models are catalogued on this site

points.desc: OpenAI's medical benchmark, built with 250+ physicians, evaluates diagnostic reasoning and safety - the clearest public yardstick for whether a model belongs anywhere near clinical work.
points.name: HealthBench measures clinical model quality

points.desc: Independent model evaluation including healthcare and medical reasoning - vendor-neutral comparison of what actually performs.
points.name: Artificial Analysis ranks models on medical tasks

points.desc: Healthcare IT research rating clinical AI vendors on real-world provider experience rather than vendor claims.
points.name: KLAS benchmarks the vendors from provider feedback

points.desc: The digital health venture research series is the standard record of funding flowing into clinical AI and where it lands.
points.name: Rock Health tracks the capital

summary: Imaging diagnostics, clinical documentation, and drug discovery lead real deployment; the evidence and governance frameworks are maturing fastest here.
